I'll plant wheat in October and maize in June, same as every year. My land is 6 mu, not too big, not too small. I work it mostly myself with my wife — our kids work in town.

For wheat, I usually buy compound fertilizer at the shop, 15-15-15 kind. I put 2 bags per mu as base fertilizer before planting — each bag is 50 jin so that's about 50 kg per mu of compound. Then at green-up in spring I spread urea, maybe 25-30 jin (about 15 kg) per mu. The old man next door does similar. Too little and the wheat stays yellow, I don't want that.

Water — I have a well, so I irrigate. Winter water once before freeze, then at jointing, and again at grain filling. Three times usually, four if spring is dry.

Spray — aphids come in May, I spray once. Sometimes twice if bad. Wheat scab I watch for at flowering.

For maize, I plant Zhengdan or similar hybrid seed, what the dealer says is good that year. Maize is stronger, needs less babying. I broadcast compound fertilizer when planting, about 40 kg per mu, then urea at big trumpet stage, 20 kg per mu. One irrigation usually enough if rain comes, two if dry. Spray once for borers.

Tillage — I rent the rotary tiller from the village, cheaper than ploughing every year. After maize harvest I chop the stalks and rotary till for wheat.

Yield — good year wheat gives me 450 kg/mu, maize about 550 kg/mu. That's what I count on.
